deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page is a draft of the part of Riemann's 1860 memoir 'Über die Fortpflanzung ebener Luftwellen von endlicher Schwingungsweite' that solves an initial discontinuity, today called the Riemann problem. The gas is barotropic, with pressure p = φ(ϱ). The Riemann invariants are r = (f(ϱ)+u)/2 and s = (f(ϱ)−u)/2, where f(ϱ) = ∫ sqrt(φ'(ϱ)) dϱ/ϱ. Hence u = r − s and f = r + s. At t = 0 the state is (u1, ϱ1) for x < 0 and (u2, ϱ2) for x > 0.

General classification. From the discontinuity there emerge, depending on the data, one of four patterns:
- two opposite shocks ('Verdichtungsstöße');
- one forward shock;
- one backward shock;
- no shock, so the motion stays continuous.
Primed quantities denote the state between or behind the shocks at the first instant.

Case of two shocks. Here ϱ' > ϱ1 and ϱ' > ϱ2. The jump conditions (mass plus momentum) give
(4) u1 − u' = sqrt((ϱ'−ϱ1)(φ(ϱ')−φ(ϱ1))/(ϱ1 ϱ')) and u' − u2 = sqrt((ϱ'−ϱ2)(φ(ϱ')−φ(ϱ2))/(ϱ2 ϱ')).
(5) u1 − u2 = (sum of the two roots).
Both roots increase with ϱ'. So two shocks are possible iff u1 − u2 > 0 and (u1−u2)^2 > (ϱ1−ϱ2)(φ(ϱ1)−φ(ϱ2))/(ϱ1ϱ2). That is the value of the right side of (5) at ϱ' = max(ϱ1, ϱ2), where the root for the denser side vanishes.

Other patterns.
- If the opposite inequalities hold (the two-rarefaction conditions), the pairs (r1, s1) and (r2, s2) separate. The forward wave moves faster, so the discontinuity disappears.
- If only the first, not the second, set of conditions holds, the data are resolved by a single forward or backward shock according as ϱ1 > ϱ2 or ϱ1 < ϱ2. In the final classification below this single shock is accompanied by a rarefaction wave (cases III and IV).

Example: Boyle's law. Take φ(ϱ) = a^2 ϱ, so f = a log ϱ, with piecewise-constant data. Four cases.

Case I: u1 − u2 > 0 and ((u1−u2)/a)^2 > (ϱ1−ϱ2)^2/(ϱ1ϱ2). Two opposite shocks form.
- For isothermal gas each root in (4) equals a(sqrt(ϱ'/ϱi) − sqrt(ϱi/ϱ')).
- [Mine] Put ϱ' = θ^2 sqrt(ϱ1ϱ2) and α = (ϱ1/ϱ2)^(1/4). Then sqrt(ϱ'/ϱ1) = θ/α and sqrt(ϱ'/ϱ2) = θα.
- So (5) becomes (u1−u2)/(a(α+1/α)) = θ − 1/θ, with θ the positive root.
- Shock speeds, from mass flux j^2 = a^2 ϱ' ϱi:
  - forward shock: dξ/dt = u2 + aθα = u' + a/(θα);
  - backward shock: dη/dt = u1 − aθ/α = u' − aα/θ.
- Solution at time t:
  - (u', ϱ') for (u1 − aθ/α)t < x < (u2 + aθα)t;
  - (u1, ϱ1) to the left;
  - (u2, ϱ2) to the right.

Case II: u1 − u2 < 0 and ((u1−u2)/a)^2 ≥ (log(ϱ1/ϱ2))^2. Two centred rarefaction waves form.
- Between them r = r1, s = s2, u = r1 − s2.
- [Mine] The conditions are exactly ϱ_mid ≤ ϱ1 and ϱ_mid ≤ ϱ2, where a log ϱ_mid = r1 + s2.
- Forward fan: s = s2, and x − (u+a)t is a function of r that vanishes because the wave is centred at x = t = 0. So u = x/t − a for (r1−s2+a)t < x < (u2+a)t, with r = r1 to the left and r = r2 to the right.
- Backward fan: r = r1, x − (u−a)t = 0. So u = x/t + a for (u1−a)t < x < (r1−s2−a)t, with s = s1 to the left and s = s2 to the right.

Case III: neither I nor II, and ϱ1 > ϱ2. A backward rarefaction and a forward shock form.
- [Mine] Across the rarefaction r' = r1. Across the shock u' − u2 = a(θ − 1/θ), with ϱ' = θ^2 ϱ2.
- This gives 2(r1−r2)/a = 2 log θ + θ − 1/θ.
- Shock speed: dξ/dt = u2 + aθ = u' + a/θ.
- Ahead of the shock (x > (u2+aθ)t) the state is (u2, ϱ2). The text breaks off at the state behind the shock.

Case IV: ϱ2 > ϱ1. The same as III, mirrored.
errors: The transcription's denominator ϱϱ' in (4) must be ϱ1ϱ' in the first formula and ϱ2ϱ' in the second, as the jump conditions require. This is likely a reading error.
The criterion '(u1−u2)^2 > (ϱ1−ϱ2)' as transcribed is incomplete. It should read (u1−u2)^2 > (ϱ1−ϱ2)(φ(ϱ1)−φ(ϱ2))/(ϱ1ϱ2).

Case I states two conditions. The first, '2ϱ(u1−u2)^2/a > (log ϱ1/ϱ2)^2', is dimensionally wrong and seems to be a garbled or struck draft. Only u1 − u2 > 0 together with ((u1−u2)/a)^2 > (ϱ1−ϱ2)^2/(ϱ1ϱ2) is needed. Since (ϱ1−ϱ2)^2/(ϱ1ϱ2) ≥ (log(ϱ1/ϱ2))^2, this condition also excludes case II.

For the formulas to be consistent, α must equal (ϱ1/ϱ2)^(1/4) and ϱ' must equal θ^2 sqrt(ϱ1ϱ2), not α = ϱ1/ϱ2 and ϱ' = θ sqrt(ϱ1ϱ2). Likewise in case III, ϱ' = θ^2 ϱ2. The manuscript probably has θθ and a fourth root; with these readings everything checks.

Conceptual remark, not a slip on this page: Riemann's shocks conserve mass and momentum with p = φ(ϱ) only, ignoring energy. This is exact for the isothermal (Boyle) example used here, but not for the adiabatic gas (the later Rankine–Hugoniot/Rayleigh critique).

results.what: Jump conditions for a barotropic gas: (u1−u')^2 = (ϱ'−ϱ1)(φ(ϱ')−φ(ϱ1))/(ϱ1ϱ')
results.modern_name: Rankine–Hugoniot conditions (mass and momentum) for the p-system
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1860 (preceded by Stokes 1848 in part; Rankine 1870 and Hugoniot 1887 added energy)

results.what: Classification of the resolution of an initial jump into two shocks, two rarefactions, or a shock plus a rarefaction, with explicit criteria
Explicit isothermal Riemann solution: the θ-equations, shock speeds, and centred rarefaction fans u = x/t ± a
results.modern_name: Exact Riemann solver for isothermal gas dynamics

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of material published in Riemann's 1860 memoir, the origin of the 'Riemann problem'. It is well known as his work.

checkable.asserts: The isothermal shock velocity jump equals a(sqrt(ϱ'/ϱ1) − sqrt(ϱ1/ϱ')).
With ϱ' = θ^2 sqrt(ϱ1ϱ2) and α = (ϱ1/ϱ2)^(1/4), equation (5) reduces to (u1−u2)/(a(α+1/α)) = θ − 1/θ.
The forward shock speed u2 + aθα equals u' + a/(θα), where u' = u2 + a(θα − 1/(θα)).

checkable.asserts: In case III, 2(r1−r2) = a log(ϱ'/ϱ2) + (u'−u2) = a(2 log θ + θ − 1/θ) when ϱ' = θ^2 ϱ2.
The two-shock threshold (ϱ1−ϱ2)^2/(ϱ1ϱ2) equals the squared isothermal shock jump at ϱ' = ϱ1.

transcription_corrections: '(u1−u2)^2 > (ϱ1−ϱ2)' should be completed with the factor (φ(ϱ1)−φ(ϱ2))/(ϱ1ϱ2).
'ϱ' = θ√(ϱ1ϱ2)' is likely 'ϱ' = θθ√(ϱ1ϱ2)', and α is likely the fourth root of ϱ1/ϱ2 rather than ϱ1/ϱ2.
In case III, 'ϱ' = θϱ2' is likely 'ϱ' = θθϱ2'.
'Wenn die letztere Falle eintritt' probably reads 'Wenn der letztere Fall eintritt'; the following sentence describes the two-rarefaction (non-shock) situation.
'Die Werthe r1 und s1, r2 und s2 trennen dann' is probably 'trennen sich dann'.
